'''Michel Henri Devoret''' ({{IPA|fr|miʃɛl dəvɔʁɛ|lang}}; born 5 March 1953)<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-10-21 |title=PRIX NOBEL DE PHYSIQUE 2025 : Parcours des lauréats |url=https://www.universalis.fr/encyclopedie/prix-nobel-de-physique-2025/3-parcours-des-laureats/ |access-date=2025-11-17 |website=Encyclopædia Universalis |language=fr-FR}}</ref> is a French–American [[physicist]]. He is Professor of Physics at the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]],<ref name="UCSBDevoret">{{Cite web |title=Michel Devoret {{!}} Department of Physics {{!}} UC Santa Barbara |url=https://www.physics.ucsb.edu/people/michel-devoret |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251007141512/https://www.physics.ucsb.edu/people/michel-devoret |archive-date=7 October 2025 |access-date=7 October 2025 |website=www.physics.ucsb.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Michel Devoret – Andrew D. White Professors-at-Large Program |url=https://adwhiteprofessors.cornell.edu/professors-at-large/michel-devoret/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250930214242/https://adwhiteprofessors.cornell.edu/professors-at-large/michel-devoret/ |archive-date=30 September 2025 |access-date=7 October 2025 |language=en-US}}</ref> and Professor Emeritus of Applied Physics at [[Yale University]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Michel Devoret |url=https://engineering.yale.edu/research-and-faculty/faculty-directory/michel-devoret |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251007123450/http://engineering.yale.edu/research-and-faculty/faculty-directory/michel-devoret |archive-date=7 October 2025 |access-date=7 October 2025 |website=Yale Engineering |language=en}}</ref> He serves as the Chief Scientist for Quantum Hardware at [[Google Quantum AI]].<ref name="GoogleDevoret">{{Cite web |title=Googler Michel Devoret awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics |url=https://blog.google/inside-google/company-announcements/googler-michel-devoret-awarded-the-nobel-prize-in-physics/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251007193339/https://blog.google/inside-google/company-announcements/googler-michel-devoret-awarded-the-nobel-prize-in-physics/ |archive-date=7 October 2025 |access-date=7 October 2025 |website=Inside Google |language=en}}</ref> He is known for the development of various [[superconducting quantum computing]] architectures, including the quantronium, the [[transmon]], and the [[Superconducting quantum computing#Fluxonium|fluxonium]].

Devoret shared the 2025 [[Nobel Prize in Physics]] with [[John Clarke (physicist)|John Clarke]] and [[John M. Martinis]] for their joint work on [[macroscopic quantum phenomena]] in [[Circuit quantum electrodynamics|superconducting circuits]].<ref name=Nobel>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m9FUkAis62s |title=Announcement of the 2025 Nobel Prize in Physics |date=7 October 2025 |last= Physics Nobel Prize|access-date=7 October 2025 |via=YouTube}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Michel Henri Devoret was born on 5 March 1953 in [[Paris]].<ref name="CDF">{{cite web |title=Michel Devoret – Biography and publications |url=https://www.college-de-france.fr/en/chair/michel-devoret-mesoscopic-physics-statutory-chair/biography |url-status=dead |publisher=Collège de France |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260316142738/https://www.college-de-france.fr/en/chair/michel-devoret-mesoscopic-physics-statutory-chair/biography |archive-date=2026-03-16 |access-date=2025-10-07}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Nobel Prize in Physics 2025 |url=https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2025/devoret/facts/ |access-date=7 October 2025 |website=NobelPrize.org |language=en-US}}</ref> He has stated that his parents were of Jewish background, even though they were not religious.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Zierler |first=David |date=April 7, 2021 |title=Devoret, Michel on 2021 April 7. |url=https://repository.aip.org/node/129778 |website=Niels Bohr Library & Archives}}</ref>

In 1975, Devoret graduated from École nationale supérieure des télécommunications (now [[Télécom Paris]]) with a degree in Engineering. He then obtained a [[postgraduate diploma]] in Quantum Optics in 1976, followed by a [[Doctor of Philosophy]] in Quantum Condensed Matter Physics in 1982, both from the University of Orsay (now [[Paris-Saclay University]]).<ref>{{Cite encyclopedia|title=Michel H. Devoret
|url=https://www.britannica.com/biography/Michel-H-Devoret|url-status=live|encyclopedia=Encyclopædia Britannica|date=2026-01-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251110082726/https://www.britannica.com/biography/Michel-H-Devoret|archive-date=2025-11-10|access-date=2026-06-14}}</ref><ref name="CDF" /> He performed his doctoral research at [[CEA Paris-Saclay|CEA Saclay]] in the group of [[Anatole Abragam]],<ref name="Hassinger">{{Cite book |last=Hassinger |first=Sebastian |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=cE8hEQAAQBAJ&dq=martinis+phd+%22advisor%22+clarke+devoret&pg=PA113 |title=The New Quantum Era |date=11 September 2024 |publisher=O'Reilly Media, Inc. |isbn=978-1-0981-4938-3 |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":3" /> under the supervision of [[Neil S. Sullivan]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite book |last=Abragam |first=A. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=WNdHAwAAQBAJ&dq=michel+devoret+neil+sullivan+abragam&pg=PA255 |title=De la physique avant toute chose |date=2000 |publisher=Odile Jacob |isbn=978-2-7381-9064-2 |language=fr}}</ref>

== Career ==
Devoret worked as a [[postdoctoral researcher]] in [[John Clarke (physicist)|John Clarke]]'s group at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], from 1982 to 1984.<ref name="CDF" /> Together, with [[John M. Martinis]], a graduate student at the time, they demonstrated for the first time the [[Phase qubit#Quantized energy levels|quantized energy levels]] of a [[Josephson effect|Josephson junction]] in 1985.<ref name="CDF" /><ref name="Hassinger"/>

Devoret then returned to France and founded the Quantronics group at the Orme des Merisiers laboratory of CEA Saclay together with {{Ill|Daniel Esteve|fr|Daniel Esteve}} and Cristian Urbina. The group measured the traversal time of tunnelling, invented an electron pump, observed the charge of Cooper pairs directly, and developed a type of [[qubit]] dubbed ''quantronium''. They also observed the [[Ramsey interferometry|Ramsey fringes]] of quantronium.<ref name="CDF" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=2025 Nobel Prize Resources |url=https://www.aip.org/nobel-prize |access-date=8 October 2025 |website=AIP |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Mooij |first=Hans |date=1 December 2004 |title=Superconducting quantum bits |url=https://physicsworld.com/superconducting-quantum-bits/ |access-date=9 October 2025 |website=Physics World |language=en-GB}}</ref>

In 1996, Devoret spent a research stay in the laboratory of {{ill|Hans Mooij|de}} at [[Delft University of Technology]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022 |title=The story of a research group at the origin of nan and quantum science in Delft. 1971-2013 |url=https://qutech.nl/wp-content/uploads/2022/05/Hans-Mooij-QT.pdf |access-date=November 17, 2025 |website=QuTech}}</ref>

Devoret became a professor at [[Yale University]] in 2002. At Yale University, [[Steven Girvin]], [[Robert J. Schoelkopf]], and Devoret devised a type of superconducting [[charge qubit]] called the [[transmon]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=7 October 2025 |title=Yale's Michel H. Devoret wins 2025 Nobel Prize in Physics {{!}} Yale News |url=https://news.yale.edu/2025/10/07/yales-michel-h-devoret-wins-2025-nobel-prize-physics |access-date=9 October 2025 |website=news.yale.edu |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Elsayyid |first=Joseph |date=6 February 2025 |title=Yale Quantum Institute marks ten years |url=https://yaledailynews.com/blog/2025/02/05/yale-quantum-institute-marks-ten-years/ |access-date=9 October 2025 |website=Yale Daily News |language=en}}</ref> In 2009, Devoret also pioneered [[Superconducting quantum computing#Fluxonium|fluxonium]],<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Manucharyan |first1=Vladimir E. |last2=Koch |first2=Jens |author3-link=Leonid Glazman |last3=Glazman |first3=Leonid I. |last4=Devoret |first4=Michel H. |title=Fluxonium: single cooper-pair circuit free of charge offsets |journal=Science |volume=326 |issue=5949 |pages=113–116 |date=2 October 2009 |publisher=American Association for the Advancement of Science |doi=10.1126/science.1175552 |url=https://www.science.org/doi/abs/10.1126/science.1175552 |pmid=19797655 |arxiv=0906.0831 |bibcode=2009Sci...326..113M }}</ref> which can be understood as a special type of [[flux qubit]]. In 2010, he also developed a microwave [[Quantum amplifier|quantum limited amplifier]] for qubit readout and sensing.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Roy |first1=Ananda |last2=Devoret |first2=Michel |date=July 2018 |title=Quantum-limited parametric amplification with Josephson circuits in the regime of pump depletion |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevB.98.045405 |journal=Phys. Rev. B |publisher=American Physical Society |volume=98 |issue=4 |arxiv=1801.10115 |bibcode=2018PhRvB..98d5405R |doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.98.045405 |article-number=045405}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=May 5, 2010 |title=Yale-designed amplifier pushes the boundary of quantum physics |url=https://news.yale.edu/2010/05/05/yale-designed-amplifier-pushes-boundary-quantum-physics |access-date=2025-10-10 |website=YaleNews |publisher=Yale University}}</ref>

He also participated in 2018 in an experiment demonstrating the interruption and reversal of quantum jumps in a superconducting [[artificial atom]], providing new insights into the dynamics of quantum measurement.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dumé |first=Isabelle |date=June 7, 2019 |title=To catch a quantum jump |url=https://physicsworld.com/a/to-catch-a-quantum-jump/ |website=Physics World}}</ref>

From 2007 to 2012, Michel Devoret held the Chair of Mesoscopic Physics at the [[Collège de France]] where his inaugural lecture, "From the Atom to Quantum Machines," illustrated the connection between fundamental quantum phenomena and emerging quantum technologies.<ref>{{Cite web |title=From atoms to quantum machines |url=https://www.college-de-france.fr/en/agenda/opening-lecture/from-atoms-to-quantum-machines/from-atoms-to-quantum-machines |access-date=November 17, 2025 |website=Collège de France}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |date=December 2008 |title=Michel Devoret, De l'atome aux machines quantiques |url=https://journals.openedition.org/lettre-cdf/672?lang=en |journal=La Lettre du Collège de France |issue=24 |via=OpenEdition.org}}</ref> He resigned in 2013.<ref name="CDF" /><ref name=":2" />

In 2023, he was named the Chief Scientist for Hardware at [[Google]] Quantum AI.<ref name="GoogleDevoret" /> In 2024, he moved to the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]] to serve as Professor of Physics.<ref name="UCSBDevoret" />
